1. These two appeals are being disposed of by this common judgment since M.A.C.M.A.No.1566 of 2016, filed by the claimants seeking for enhancement of compensation and M.A.C.M.A.No.2328 of 2016, filed by the Insurance Company challenging the compensation awarded, both are directed against the very same Award and Decree, dated 04.07.2015 passed in O.P.No.1508 of 2013, on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- II Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court,
Hyderabad (for short, "the Tribunal").
2.

entities.text:
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- II Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court,
Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter be referred as they were arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the claim petitioners, who are the wife and children of Late V.Shankar Rao (hereinafter be referred as "the deceased"), filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of the death of the deceased in a motor vehicle accident caused with the Car bearing No.AP-10M-9068 on 03.02.2013.

It is stated by the petitioners that on 03.02.2013 at MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 about 19.30 hours, when the deceased was proceeding from his house on his bike bearing No.AP-25N-3545 towards Apna Bazar and on the way, when he reached near Apna Bazar Super Market, the Car bearing No.AP-10M-9068, which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction and dashed the motorcycle of the deceased , due to which he fell down and received grievous injuries and immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital,
Nizamabad, in Ambulance, from where, he was shifted to Gandhi Hospital, Secunderabad and while undergoing treatment, he died on 09.02.2013.
4.
Based on a complaint, Police of Nizamabad Police Station, registered a case in Crime No.21 of 2013, under Section 304-A IPC against the driver of Car bearing No.AP-10M-9068.

It is further stated by the petitioners that prior to accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged 42 years and working as Sales Executive at Hindustan Lever Company Limited and was getting income @
Rs.6,00,000/- per annum and contributing the same for welfare and maintenance of the family.

Due to his sudden and untimely death, the petitioners lost their source of income and were put to severe hardship and hence, filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- along with costs and interest MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 against the respondent Nos.1 & 2,
who are the owner and insurer of the crime vehicle i.e., Car bearing No.AP-10M-9068.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1/Owner of Car bearing No.AP-10M-9068, filed his counter denying the averments made in the claim petition including, age, occupation, income, injuries sustained to him and death of the deceased.

He further contended that as the subject crime vehicle is insured with 2nd respondent and the policy was valid from 11.12.2012 to 10.12.2013, hence, respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and that the claim of compensation is excess and exorbitant and prayed to dismiss the claim against it.
6.

Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed its counter denying the averments made in the claim petition including rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Car, age, occupation, income of the deceased and contended that there was delay of 6 days in lodging the complaint and that the crime vehicle was being plied without having valid permit and fitness certificate and that respondent No.1 had failed to comply the statutory conditions mentioned under Section 134 (c) of M.V.Act and that the claim of compensation is excess and hence, prayed to dismiss the claim against it.
MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 7.

Based on the pleadings made by both the parties, the learned Tribunal had framed the following issues for conducting trial:-
(i) Whether the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing No.AP-10M-9068 causing death of V.Shankar Rao?
( ii )
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
(iii) To what relief?
8.
On behalf of the petitioners, PWs1 to 3 were examined and Exs.A1 to A7 and Ex.X1 were marked.
On behalf of Respondent No.2/Insurance Company, RW1 was examined and Exs.B1 to B3 were marked.

9. After considering the entire evidence and documents available on record, the learned Tribunal had partly allowed the claim petition of the petitioners by granting compensation of Rs.11,98,472/-
along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit payable by both the Respondent Nos.1 & 2.
Challenging the same, the present appeals came to be filed by the claimants and Insurance Company respectively.
MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 10.
Heard Sri T.Viswarupachary, learned counsel for appellants/claimants and Sri Kondadi Ajay Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
Perused the record.

sentences.text: The contentions of the learned counsel for appellants in M.A.C.M.A.No.1566 of 2016 are that the learned Tribunal had not granted any amount towards future prospects and had also not awarded any amount on the counts of loss of love and affection to children, non-pecuniary damages and transportation charges, loss of estate and loss of spousal consortium and hence prayed for enhancement of compensation.
Learned counsel also relied upon certain decisions reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, 2013 ACJ 1403 and 2015 ACJ 1286 in support of his contentions.

12. On the other hand, learned Standing Counsel representing the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company and also the appellant in M.A.C.M.A.No.2328 of 2016 submitted that the learned Tribunal ought to have seen that there was delay of 6 days in lodging the complaint before police station;
ought to have seen that the driver of the vehicle failed to produce necessary particulars as envisaged under Section 134(c) of M.V.Act; ought to have seen that the claimants did not produce any evidence nor examined anyone in relation to the employment of the deceased and his earning MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 capacity; ought to have seen that there is negligence on part of the deceased himself who contributed to the accident and hence prayed to allow the Appeal by setting aside the order of learned Tribunal.

13. Now the points that emerges for determination are,
(i). Whether the order passed by the learned Tribunal suffers from any irregularity?
(ii). Whether the appellants/claim petitioners are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
POINTS:-
14.
It is pertinent to state that the wife of the deceased was examined as PW1 and reiterated the contents made in the claim petition.

As she is not an eye witness to the incident, she got examined PW2, an eye witness to the incident who deposed that due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car, the accident took place and the deceased received grievous injuries and was shifted to Government Hospital, Nizamabad, from there to Gandhi Hospital, Secunderbad and while undergoing treatment, he died.

PW3 is the Mandal Surveyor at Tahsildar Officer, Navipet, who deposed that the deceased used to cultivate lands on Koul basis and used to earn income not less than Rs.5,000/- and Ex.A7 is the certificate issued by their office.
Apart from adducing oral evidence, the claim petitioners also got marked Exs
. A1 to A7 MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 and Ex
.X1 on their behalf.

Ex . A1-Copy of FIR shows that Traffic Police Station, Nizamabad District, registered a case in Crime No.21 of 2013 under Section 304-A IPC, conducted investigation and laid Ex.A4-Charge sheet against the driver of the offending Car for his rash and negligent driving which resulted in an accident and thereby caused death of the deceased.
Ex.A2 is the Inquest report.
Ex.A3 is the Post mortem examination report wherein, the cause of death of deceased was mentioned as "due to Head Injury".
Ex. A5
- MVI report also shows that the accident had not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex . A6
is the Pay Slip of the deceased issued by HDFC Bank for the month of January 2010 showing the net pay as "Rs.5031/-".
Ex . A7
is the Certificate given by Tahsildar, Navipet, showing the estimated amount of Rs.5,85,000/- that the deceased used to derive from the two crops.

sentences.text:
Therefore, from the evidence of PW2, an eye-witness to the incident coupled with the documents marked under Exs.A1 to A5, it is made clear that the death of the deceased was due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Car.
16. Coming to the evidence of RW1, who is working as Executive (Legal) in the Insurance Company,
admitted in his evidence that the crime vehicle was insured with their company vide Ex.B1- Insurance Policy.
Ex.B2 is the Death Summary of the deceased.
MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 Ex.B3 is the rough sketch.

Therefore, from the evidence of RW1 coupled with the document marked under Ex.B1, it clearly shows that Respondent No.1 was the registered owner of the said crime vehicle Car bearing No.AP-10M-9068 which was duly insured with Respondent No.2 under Ex.B1-Insurance Policy which is valid as on the date of accident.

17. It is the contention of the learned Standing Counsel for Appellant/Insurance Company in MACMA.No.2238 of 2016 that the learned Tribunal failed to see that there was delay of 6 days in lodging the complaint before police station.

In this regard, it is pertinent to refer to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ravi v. Badrinaryan 1, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court at Para No.21 held as under:-
"21.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.

Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of (2011) 4 SCC 693 MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.

In such circumstances,
the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."

18. In the instant case, the reason stated by the petitioners for delay in lodging FIR is that as there was nobody to look after her husband, she remained with him in the hospital and could not lodge any complaint in the police station and therefore, there occurred delay of 6 days in giving complaint before police station.
Having found the said reason to be satisfactory, the Tribunal had considered the claim petition of the petitioners.

It is also admitted fact that delay in lodging of FIR cannot be a ground to dismiss the claim petition as the family members will be engaged in providing necessary treatment to the injured instead of rushing to police station for giving a complaint regarding the accident.

19. 4 as envisaged under Section 134(c) of M.V.Act.

sentences.text: In this regard, it is pertinent to refer to the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Rukmani v.New India MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 Assurance Co 2 wherein, it has been held that it is the burden of the insurance company to establish that the driver was not having a valid licence to drive the vehicle.

entities.text: Rukmani v.New India MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 Assurance Co 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case the insurance company though had relied upon the evidence of the Investigating Officer, but the insurance company did not summon the driver and had not produced any record from the Regional Transport Authority, therefore, the Apex Court took a view that the insurance company cannot be exonerated.

The Division Bench of this Court in the matter of Jagdish v.Rajkumar 3, has taken a view that when no record of the Licensing Authority is proved by the insurer it cannot be assumed that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid license to drive the vehicle.
Even if no driving license is produced on notice to owner and driver, then also no adverse inference against them can be drawn.

21. In the present case, the insurance company though had taken a defence in the written statement that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid license to drive the vehicle, but no evidence was produced by the insurance company to establish the said fact.
The insurance company has not produced any certificate from the concerned Transport Authority to establish the said fact.

No investigation report has been placed on record by 1999 ACJ 171 (SC) 2002 ACJ 1124 (MP) MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 the insurance company to show that there is any infirmity in the driving license of the driver of offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 22. Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, it is the case of the claimants that the deceased was aged 42 years and was working as Sales Executive at Hindustan Lever Company Limited and used to get income of Rs.6,00,000/- per annum.
In support of their contention, they filed Ex.A6-Payslip of the deceased showing the net salary as Rs.5,031.

Further, the petitioners also examined one Sravan Kumar, Mandal Surveyor, who deposed that the deceased used to get income not less than Rs.5,000/- by cultivating the lands on Koul basis and also issued Ex.A7 certificate to that effect.

Therefore, considering the above said two documents marked under Exs.A6 & A7, the learned Tribunal fixed the income of the deceased @ Rs.10,031/- per month, deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses, applied relevant multiplier and calculated compensation which arrived at Rs.11,98,472/- .
23.
A perusal of the impugned judgment shows that the learned Tribunal had not awarded future prospects to the established income of the deceased.

This Court, by relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others 4, is inclined to add 25% to the established income towards future prospects as the deceased being 42 years old.

entities.text: National Insurance Company MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others 4

sentences.text: Then the future monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.12,539/-.
If 1/3rd of the income is deducted towards his personal expenses as the number of dependants are 3, then the net monthly income comes to Rs.8,359/- and the annual incomes comes to Rs.1,00,308/-.
As the deceased was aged 42 years at the time of accident, the appropriate multiplier is '14' as per the decision of the Apex Court in Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 5 .

sentences.text: Thus, by applying the multiplier '14', the total loss of dependency comes to Rs.14,04,312/-.

Further, the learned Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.25,000/- towards Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Smt V. Vani on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184359445/
5 funeral expenses, Rs.25,000/- towards loss of estate Rs.25,000/- towards loss of consortium, which this Court considers desirable and is not inclined to interfere with the same.

Nanu Ram @ Chuhru 2017 ACJ 2700 2009 (6) SCC 121 MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 Ram and others 6.

Thus, in all, the claimants are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.15,59,312/- which is calculated as under:-

Monthly income Rs.10,031 - 2 Future prospects - 25% 3 Income arrived after Rs.80,248/- Rs.1,00,308/-
1/3rd deduction 4 Applying multiplier Rs.11,23,472/- Rs.14,04,312/- 5 Conventional heads Rs.75,000/- -

6 Parental consortium - Rs.80,000/-
7 TOTAL Rs.11,98,472/- Rs.15,59,312/-
.
24.

In the result, M.A.C.M.A.No.2338 of 2016, filed by Insurance Company is dismissed and M.A.C.M.A.No.1566 of 2016 is allowed by enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.11,98,472/- to Rs.15,59,312/- which shall carry interest @ 7.5% per annum payable by both the Respondent Nos.1 & 2 jointly and severally within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

On such deposit, the appellants in MACMA.No.1566 of 2016 are entitled to withdraw the same as per (2018) 18 SCC 130 MGP,J MACMA.Nos.1566 and 2328 of 2016 the apportionment made by the learned Tribunal by paying deficit Court fee.
There shall be no order as to costs.
25. Miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.
